english: When, shepherd, was this little lamb born? It was born at night; that white ewe bore it. Why does it cry? It is hungry now; it sucks at its mother's udder. May I lift it? Do not lift it on this day; its leg is soft. When it grows strong, I will lead it to the field. Now you will be its shepherd.

english: Elder, in my dream the lambs ran toward the hill. I was afraid for my father's (flock). Boy, do not fear; let us see them. Take the dog with you. Why do I take it? What the eye has not seen, the dog's nose sees. I count them. How many are there? There are four lambs. Now none is missing. Do not sleep in the field.

Grandfather, tell me the names. What of this one? I will tell you of it. Where have you seen it? I have seen it with my own eyes. You learned quickly. Now he spoke the name of this one. He stood up for me on foot and feet(?).

Deiwogenes, wash your feet. I do not wash myself; it is cold. You walk black (dirty). Wash them, and I give you mead. Mead? Now I wash. Wash your knees and shoulders too. Look at me: now my feet are white. Now give me the mead. There it is.

Sister, I am hungry. What are you cooking? I am cooking meat on the fire. Now give it to me. It is still raw; it is boiling. Go and fetch water from the river. I fetched water. Now may I eat? Now eat; do not burn your mouth. It is still hot and sweet.

Father, I shall plow the field this day. Now yoke the two oxen. I yoked them. Is the yoke straight? It is straight. Now hold the plow and drive them. My furrow is not straight. Look at one piece of wood (a mark). Son, are you tired? I am not tired. I will become a man. Now plow, and in the evening we eat together.
